🚨🇲🇽 <u>ARMY, NATIONAL GUARD AND FGR DISMANTLE SINALOA CARTEL ARSENAL IN SONORA</u>

Mexican federal forces dismantled a Sinaloa cartel weapons depot in San Luis Río Colorado, Sonora, seizing 274,800 cartridges, 81 long guns and 128 magazines. The haul included 72 AK-47 rifles and a Browning .50 caliber machine gun designed to destroy armored vehicles and aircraft.

The stash house, located in Colonia Federal, belonged to Los Rusos — the cell operating under Ismael Zambada Sicairos' faction — and was identified by the Security Cabinet as a key logistics node for the border region. Found and taken down by Mexican military intelligence. No foreign agents needed. (Regeneración)

🔥🇲🇽 <u>CERO IMPUNIDAD: 13 FEDERAL OFFICIALS SANCTIONED ACROSS 9 AGENCIES</u>

Mexico's Anticorruption and Good Government Secretariat sanctioned 13 public servants from nine federal agencies — Pemex, CFE, IMSS, Sedena, DIF, customs (ANAM), INDEP, the Port of Manzanillo and the Health Secretariat — after concluded internal investigations.

Among the cases: an IMSS doctor in Querétaro barred for three months for failing to diagnose and treat a patient who later died; a DIF childcare worker suspended for mistreating a minor; and three AICM customs agents suspended for skipping full luggage inspections.

"The Secretariat will defend its resolutions with the same firmness with which they were issued: attached to law, backed by evidence, and putting the rights of affected persons first," the agency stated. (El Soberano)

🚨🇲🇽 <u>TRUMP FREES NARCO-PRESIDENT JOH — WHILE LECTURING MEXICO ON CARTELS</u>

Juan Orlando Hernández flew home to Honduras Sunday on a private jet from Miami, a free man. He was sentenced in 2024 to 45 years in the US for moving more than 400 tons of cocaine with the Sinaloa cartel — then Trump pardoned him last December, and a US appeals court annulled his conviction in April.

This is the same Washington that brands Mexican cartels "terrorists," demands extraditions of Mexican officials, and accuses Sheinbaum's government of narco ties without a shred of evidence. Four hundred tons of cocaine buys you a pardon. Mexican sovereignty gets you threats. (El Soberano)
banner: NARCO HYPOCRISY: JOH FREED BY TRUMP

🇲🇽🇨🇺 <u>"GRACIAS MÉXICO": DÍAZ-CANEL THANKS MASS CDMX MARCH FOR CUBA</u>

Thousands marched Sunday in Mexico City — from the Hemiciclo a Juárez to the old US embassy — against the tightening US blockade of Cuba, on the 73rd anniversary of the Moncada assault. Solidarity actions were reported in other Mexican states as well.

Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel answered: "Gracias México. Once again at the vanguard of the dignity of Our America. To all who marched for Cuba this July 26, the grateful embrace of a people that always found solidarity in the noble and generous Aztec land."

Cuba's foreign ministry and its ambassador in Mexico also thanked the mobilization — the ambassador posted a photo of the giant banner unfurled at the Ángel de la Independencia: "Petróleo para Cuba." (La Jornada)

🇲🇽⚡ <u>CFE: POWER OUTAGES DOWN 39% IN TWO YEARS</u>

Mexico's electric grid is delivering measurable results. CFE director Emilia Calleja reports power interruptions fell 39% in the first half of 2026 versus the same period of 2024, with restoration times also sharply reduced — the payoff of a "historic investment" in transmission and distribution networks that for decades took a back seat to generation.

"The future of our national electric system depends on modern, robust and intelligent grids — grids that integrate new energy sources, anticipate failures and respond better to natural phenomena," Calleja said in Acapulco, the city that lived through Hurricane Otis. (La Jornada)

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>OIL BACK OVER $100 — MEXICAN MIX HITS $91.68</u>

Brent crude tore past $100 a barrel this week — peaking at $105.32, its first trip above $100 in two months — as the US-Iran standoff keeps the Strait of Hormuz on edge. El Economista's weekly markets wrap put it plainly: "Petróleo rebasa US$100."

Mexico's export mix rode the wave to $91.68 a barrel — 18% above the $77.30 assumed in the 2026 budget. More dollars for Pemex and Hacienda, while the 24-peso gasoline cap holds at the pump.

🇲🇽🌽 <u>MEXICO CITY OPENS THE "UTOPIA OF CORN" TO DEFEND NATIVE MAIZE</u>

Mexico City just inaugurated the Utopía Centli — the Utopia of Corn — in the Indigenous town of San Miguel Topilejo, Tlalpan.

A 253-million-peso public complex built around a Native Corn Protection Center: seed house, germplasm bank and a lab dedicated to keeping native varieties free of transgenics. Its 50,000 square meters bring free healthcare, sports, culture and childcare to 29,000 residents.

Centli means maíz in náhuatl — the crop Mexico gave the world, protected as public heritage instead of a corporate patent.
banner: CDMX: 'UTOPIA OF CORN' FOR NATIVE SEEDS

🇲🇽🏆 <u>ISAAC DEL TORO, FIRST MEXICAN EVER ON THE TOUR DE FRANCE PODIUM</u>

History for Mexican cycling: Isaac del Toro, the 22-year-old from Ensenada, just finished third overall at the Tour de France — something no Mexican had ever achieved. Only three had even raced the Tour before him.

He also won the white jersey as the race's best young rider, sealing it on the slopes of Alpe d'Huez.

Back home, thousands packed the Ángel de la Independencia to celebrate, and President Sheinbaum joined the congratulations.
banner: DEL TORO: 3RD AT TOUR DE FRANCE

🇲🇽🌎 <u>MILEI ACCUSES MEXICO OF FUNDING "ANTI-ARGENTINA CAMPAIGN" — ZERO PROOF</u>

Argentina's Javier Milei accused Mexico, Brazil and the US Democratic Party of financing an "anti-Argentina campaign" during the World Cup — no documents, no evidence, just a radio rant.

"¿Sabe quién puso más plata en esta campaña antiargentina? El gobierno de Brasil. El 25 por ciento de los recursos salió de ahí," Milei told Radio Mitre, before claiming it "también fue financiada por México."

Brazil has already recalled its ambassador from Buenos Aires. Milei offered nothing to back any of it up.
📸 Supervisión de pozos radiales — Acapulco, Guerrero, 26 de julio de 2026
